scenes.narration: Okay, day two. Yesterday we built a list of fruits. Today is almost the same thing, with one tiny change that matters a lot.
Look at this line. Square brackets make a list. Now I swap them for round brackets. That's it, that's a tuple. Same fruits, different rules.
Let's test those rules. Say I try to change the first fruit to kiwi. Watch what Python does.
And there it is. A TypeError. Python is basically saying, a tuple cannot be changed. Honestly, that's the feature. When data should never change, a tuple protects it from you.

output: TypeError: 'tuple' object does not support item assignment

scenes.narration: Quick recap. Round brackets, fixed data. Square brackets, data you can change. Pick the right one, and the next person who reads your code knows exactly what you meant.

props.title: Recap
items: Use lists when data must change
